scenes.intent: Establish the core mismatch the method must solve.
scenes.claim: ThinkSR starts from a mismatch between thought and pixels.
scenes.narration: A compact thought state is efficient, but super-resolution asks for a value at every spatial position. The method needs a way to keep dense image detail while still using compact reasoning.

objects.text: ThinkSR starts from a mismatch between thought and pixels.

scenes.claim: A persistent carrier keeps dense information available.
scenes.narration: ThinkSR adds a dense carrier that persists while the compact process reads from it. The same carrier is updated, so spatial information remains available across thought steps.

objects.text: A persistent carrier keeps dense information available.

scenes.intent: Explain the equation that creates the dense carrier and windows.
scenes.claim: The low-resolution image becomes features, then windows.
scenes.narration: The encoder turns the low-resolution input into a dense feature field. A windowing operator then partitions that field into windows for the shared process to handle.

objects.text: The low-resolution image becomes features, then windows.

scenes.claim: The full model is a dense path with shared ticks inside.
scenes.narration: The architecture begins with an encoder, moves through windows, and applies shared DQ-CTM ticks before decoding. The dense carrier gives the compact ticking process something spatial to read and revise.

objects.text: The full model is a dense path with shared ticks inside.
Dense state carries through the path

scenes.intent: Place DQ-CTM against CTM and window-wise adaptation.
scenes.claim: DQ-CTM is the adaptation built for dense output.
scenes.narration: The comparison separates plain CTM from a window-wise adaptation and DQ-CTM. ThinkSR uses the dense-query version to make compact thought usable for image reconstruction.

objects.text: DQ-CTM is the adaptation built for dense output.
Dense queries connect thought to pixels

scenes.intent: Explain why repeated shared ticks can refine the dense carrier.
scenes.claim: Shared ticks repeatedly revise the same dense state.
scenes.narration: The carrier is not discarded after one pass; it is read and updated over ticks. This makes refinement an iterative process rather than a one-shot mapping.

objects.text: Shared ticks repeatedly revise the same dense state.

scenes.intent: Use the progress figure to show iterative reconstruction over ticks.
scenes.claim: Reconstruction is shown improving across ticks T zero to T four.
scenes.narration: The reconstruction figure tracks outputs from T zero through T four beside bicubic and ground truth. The visual evidence frames ThinkSR as a progressive reconstruction process.

objects.text: Reconstruction is shown improving across ticks T zero to T four.

scenes.intent: Explain the error-map evidence without inventing numeric values.
scenes.claim: Error maps test the same crops with one shared scale.
scenes.narration: The paper compares absolute-error maps on the same crops, using one colour scale. That matters because the visual comparison is held to a common reference.

objects.text: Error maps test the same crops with one shared scale.

scenes.intent: Show that DQ-CTM-SR is competitive with listed CNN baselines.
scenes.claim: DQ-CTM-SR sits with the CNN baselines on average score.
scenes.narration: Against CARN, IMDN, and RFDN, DQ-CTM-SR is in the same narrow average range. Its reported average is twenty eight point nine eight three.

objects.text: DQ-CTM-SR sits with the CNN baselines on average score.
The CNN group is tightly clustered

scenes.intent: Show that CATANet leads the reported table and matches the stated limitation.
scenes.claim: The reported lightweight transformer remains ahead.
scenes.narration: CATANet reports the highest average in the table, twenty nine point four eight two. DQ-CTM-SR trails that result, matching the paper's summary that recent lightweight transformers remain ahead.

objects.text: The reported lightweight transformer remains ahead.

scenes.intent: Show the cost profile in parameters from the benchmark table.
scenes.claim: The compact idea does not make the model smallest.
scenes.narration: The table reports DQ-CTM-SR at one point one two nine million parameters. That is smaller than CARN, but larger than IMDN, RFDN, and CATANet.

objects.text: The compact idea does not make the model smallest.
Parameter cost sits in the middle

scenes.intent: Summarize problem, idea, outcome, and cost.
scenes.claim: ThinkSR trades compact reasoning for a dense carrier.
scenes.narration: The problem is that compact thought alone is too small for dense reconstruction. The idea is to preserve a dense carrier while compact ticks read and update it. The result is competitive with CNN baselines, but it still trails the recent lightweight transformer result and is not the smallest model.

objects.text: ThinkSR trades compact reasoning for a dense carrier.
